optimization_surface.summary: Optimize the execution of a fixed pretrained 28-layer patch-latent decoder. The worker interprets candidate JSON graphs, including composable operators, branch partitioning, prefix reuse, tensor layout and bounded Inductor regions. Python builders are explanatory artifacts and are never imported by the Verifier. This is an executable method space, not a list of tunable constants.
modifiable: The data-only layer graph, topological composition and output
Stage versus prefix intermediate lifetimes within the fixed budget
Up to 16 homogeneous contiguous regions compiled by the fixed backend
fixed: Pretrained BF16 checkpoint and 28-layer decoder, final RMS norm and projection
Public/Hidden inputs, sampling protocol, quality gates and timing aggregation
Trusted interpreter, compiler/backend flags, numerical worker and role-specific queues
optimization_surface.metric_and_gate: Minimize paired decoder latency; score=(B-T)/B, U=0, without clipping. Formal: six Hidden prompts, seeds 101/202/303, 256 stages and three repetitions per prompt. Median per prompt then mean within seed then across seeds. Every-stage and autonomous final-latent errors <=0.001; peak allocation <=34 GiB. Quality failure scores -1 separately. Reference must meet [0.15,0.8] and improvement >=3 sample sigma_B.

baseline_reference.baseline_method: The unchanged Starter emits the published eager dense dual-branch decoder DAG: separate text/image normalizations, Q/K/V projections and MLPs, eager attention, masked branch mixing and residuals. It uses all fixed pretrained layers and no optimization/training. The evaluator checks its predictions against the supplied published layer implementation. The formal Baseline is the paired Starter measurement, not a random, broken or separately weakened anchor.
baseline_reference.reference_method: The author Reference preserves the dense graph and marks seven text-branch nodes as prefix lifetime, reusing their first values within a prompt rollout. Each repetition/prompt resets the caches, and the first timed decoder forward includes reconstruction. Both sides share checkpoint, device, cases, seeds, warmup, stage count and numerical gates; no training or fine-tuning is involved. This Reference is distinct from the more elaborate GPT/Seed selected graphs.
baseline_reference.metric: Mean of per-seed decoder rollout latency (ms)
baseline_reference.improvement_summary: Recomputed from all three formal seed results and independently from the 4608 raw timing rows: delta=24703.31286112468 ms; sigma_B=180.57194646667463 ms; delta/sigma_B=136.8059288527622; normalized score=0.422766800733905. Each seed improves. Remaining Reference latency is much larger than 3 sigma_B. These are stochastic latency measurements of one fixed checkpoint, not independent training seeds.
baseline_reference.quality_gate_summary: The existing formal Oracle job has 18 paired repetitions, 4608 unique case/repetition/stage records, six final-latent files, zero recorded stage/final error, successful CUDA child exit and a supplied independent CPU audit. Numerical aggregation was recalculated here without executing submission code. GPU stdout is explicitly unavailable; per-seed run.log files repeat the actual whole-job CPU audit stdout, with scope disclosed. Existing Trial stdout and raw records are present; no independent GPU rerun is claimed.

budget_comparability.facts: Same device/checkpoint, six cases, 256 stages and three repeats. Alternating per-stage B/R order; both caches reset before timing; prefix reconstruction included. Fixed protocol and sampler apply to both roles.
